positive: Many Samsung Fold owners say they are happy with their current phones and see Apple's entry as validation of foldables, not a threat.
Several Samsung users admit being impressed by Apple's first foldable, especially its screen, fold transition and Apple Pencil support.
Some commenters criticise Samsung for dropping stylus support, water resistance and flex mode, and hope Apple's entry pushes Samsung to improve.
negative: Many commenters say Apple is late to foldables and copying Samsung's years-old designs and features, so the product doesn't feel like a true first generation.
Several criticize Samsung's own foldables as having fragile screens, buggy software, slowdowns and held-back features, though some admit they are stuck with Samsung.
Others complain the Apple device is too expensive, too heavy or too small compared with the Samsung Fold, and mock its price.

positive: Many viewers are impressed that the crease is barely visible or not noticeable at all, and see it as better than expected.
negative: Many dislike the matte, anti-reflective inner screen, saying it looks washed out, grainy or inaccurate in colour compared with the glossy outer display.
Some see the matte finish as a way to hide the crease, and say Apple avoids drawing attention to the crease or hinge.
Commenters are split on the inner camera: some prefer an under-display camera despite worse quality, others say it looks poor and should be avoided.

positive: Many commenters say the open and close animation is smooth, clean and polished, and that the designers deserve recognition or a reward.
Several Samsung fans and Apple skeptics admit the animation is impressive, including the effect that makes the front panel look see-through.
Some see it as a signature Apple touch that could help sell the phone, and one notes it hints at angle-aware apps.
negative: Many commenters say the price is far too high, especially with everyday living costs rising, and some refuse to buy it at that level.
Several note it costs much more in other countries, with multiple regions mentioned as being well above the US price.
Others mock the folding animation as a weak headline feature, calling it an underwhelming blur effect and a sign Apple lacks innovation, with durability and repair costs also questioned.

positive: Many commenters on Pro or Pro Max phones say they plan to switch to the Duo, often trading in an older device.
Fans value a larger screen that folds small, since it could replace carrying a tablet or laptop on trips.
Supporters say the Duo isn't meant as a Pro, and casual users don't miss the cameras; a few hope for a Pro version.
negative: Many commenters see the Duo's price as too high, especially in some regions, and say they would stay with their current phone or choose a Pro Max.
Several are wary of buying a first-generation foldable and plan to wait for a later Duo or Pro version, or say the inner display wouldn't suit how they use their phone.

positive: Several left-handed viewers say they can adapt to the layout and still want the device, treating handedness as a minor issue.
Button and toolbar placement is praised as practical: top volume keys suit pocket access, one-handed screenshots and tablet-style use, and the side toolbar saves screen space.
Commenters like the size and form factor, saying it is neither too small folded nor too large open, and see uses in reading, navigation and gaming.
negative: Left-handed users feel the design disregards them, with some saying they would dislike the device or be expected to switch hands.
Several commenters say the phone is heavy and wide when folded, and a case adds more bulk, making one-handed use hard.
Some note that the layout puts content or the text field near the hinge, which makes everyday use awkward.

positive: Many commenters say they are ready to buy, seeing the foldable as a way to replace both a phone and a small tablet.
Several accept trade-offs such as no telephoto camera or Touch ID, valuing the large screen, polished software and design more.
Some plan to add extra protection like AppleCare, and one comment says rival foldables offer better specs for less money.
negative: Several doubt the premium is justified, noting missing camera quality, modest storage for the cost, and features that seem basic or not new.
Some question demand and durability, citing concerns about the hinge and glass wearing out and whether people want a foldable at all.

positive: Many commenters say they are excited and plan to buy or pre-order the Duo, often after waiting a long time for an Apple foldable.
Viewers praise the design, premium materials and polished open/close feel, and see it as a rare interesting, different iPhone.
Some value real multitasking and larger-screen features, including Apple Pencil support, while a few Android users express admiration despite debate over who copied whom.
negative: Many commenters are skeptical of the foldable's hype, saying Apple is late, short on ideas, and that fans are too easily impressed.
Commenters see the high price and heavy first-generation design as reasons to wait for a lighter, improved later model.
Several worry about the foldable screen's durability and see little need for a foldable, citing past Apple missteps and incomplete details like battery capacity.

elements.text: Example of the Slack digest, to show the format. Figures are illustrative and not guaranteed to be accurate. Data through 2026-10-05. Ask a follow-up: mention the app or message it.

examples.q: Which channel sizes break out most, and are their audiences happy? Give n.
examples.a:
Small channels break out most. 22 of 57 small-channel videos with a baseline (39%) outperformed, versus 7 of 37 mid-size videos (19%) and 0 of 17 large-channel videos. Average relative lift follows the same order: 7.0 for small, 1.3 for mid, and 0.6 for large.

Audiences are net positive in every group, but mid-size is the happiest:
- Small: net +18 (45% positive, 27% negative), n=727 product-side comments.
- Mid: net +30 (52% positive, 22% negative), n=433.
- Large: net +11 (40% positive, 29% negative), n=199.

Caveat: the small group's average lift may be pulled up by a few big hits, and large-channel results rest on only 17 videos with a baseline.
examples.sql:
WITH v AS (
  SELECT c.video_id, p.rel_lift, p.outperformer,
    CASE WHEN cr.tier IN ('nano <50k','micro 50-250k') THEN 'small'
         WHEN cr.tier='mid 250k-1M' THEN 'mid'
         WHEN cr.tier IN ('macro 1-5M','mega 5M+') THEN 'large' END AS size_group
  FROM content c
  JOIN creators cr ON cr.channel_id=c.channel_id
  JOIN performance p ON p.video_id=c.video_id
  WHERE c.topic='duo' AND c.format!='official'
),
lift AS (
  SELECT size_group,
    COUNT(*) AS n_videos,
    SUM(CASE WHEN outperformer IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS n_with_baseline,
    ROUND(AVG(outperformer),3) AS outperformer_rate,
    ROUND(AVG(rel_lift),3) AS avg_rel_lift
  FROM v WHERE size_group IS NOT NULL GROUP BY size_group
),
sent AS (
  SELECT v.size_group,
    COUNT(*) AS n_product_side,
    ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN m.sentiment='positive' THEN 1.0 ELSE 0 END),3) AS pct_positive,
    ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN m.sentiment='negative' THEN 1.0 ELSE 0 END),3) AS pct_negative,
    ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN m.sentiment='positive' THEN 1.0 ELSE 0 END)-AVG(CASE WHEN m.sentiment='negative' THEN 1.0 ELSE 0 END),3) AS net_sentiment
  FROM comments m JOIN v ON v.video_id=m.video_id
  WHERE m.lang='en' AND m.trivial=0 AND m.target IN ('product','price_value','competitor')
    AND v.size_group IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY v.size_group
)
SELECT l.size_group, l.n_videos, l.n_with_baseline, l.outperformer_rate, l.avg_rel_lift,
  s.n_product_side, s.pct_positive, s.pct_negative,
  CASE WHEN s.n_product_side>=10 THEN s.net_sentiment END AS net_sentiment
FROM lift l LEFT JOIN sent s ON s.size_group=l.size_group
ORDER BY l.outperformer_rate DESC
LIMIT 40

examples.q: Which content formats work best for mid-sized channels?
examples.a:
First impressions look like the best bet for mid-sized channels, and they have the most data. Across 15 videos, average relative lift was 1.64, 33% outperformed their baseline, and net sentiment was +33 (54% positive, 21% negative, n=193 comments).

Explainer/tips had the highest lift at 2.23 and net sentiment of +40 (56% positive, 16% negative, n=45 comments). But that is only 3 videos, with 1 outperformer, so it's tentative.

Comparisons were solid: lift 1.56, 1 of 5 videos outperformed, net +33 (n=63 comments).

Upgrade advice (6 videos, lift 0.64) and keynote recaps (4 videos, lift 0.84) had no outperformers. Their net sentiment was +27 and +18.

The meme short and durability test each have just 1 video, so there's nothing to conclude from them.

Caveat: most formats have very small n, and these are associations, not proof that format drives performance.
examples.sql: WITH v AS (SELECT c.video_id, c.format, p.rel_lift, p.outperformer FROM content c JOIN creators cr ON cr.channel_id=c.channel_id JOIN performance p ON p.video_id=c.video_id WHERE c.topic='duo' AND c.format!='official' AND cr.tier='mid 250k-1M'), s AS (SELECT v.format, COUNT(*) AS n_comments, SUM(m.sentiment='positive') AS pos, SUM(m.sentiment='negative') AS neg FROM v JOIN comments m ON m.video_id=v.video_id WHERE m.lang='en' AND m.trivial=0 AND m.target IN ('product','price_value','competitor') GROUP BY v.format) SELECT v.format, COUNT(*) AS n_videos, SUM(v.rel_lift IS NOT NULL) AS n_with_baseline, ROUND(AVG(v.rel_lift),3) AS avg_rel_lift, ROUND(AVG(v.outperformer),3) AS outperformer_rate, s.n_comments AS n_product_side_comments, CASE WHEN s.n_comments>=10 THEN ROUND(1.0*s.pos/s.n_comments,3) END AS pct_positive, CASE WHEN s.n_comments>=10 THEN ROUND(1.0*s.neg/s.n_comments,3) END AS pct_negative, CASE WHEN s.n_comments>=10 THEN ROUND(1.0*(s.pos-s.neg)/s.n_comments,3) END AS net_sentiment FROM v LEFT JOIN s ON s.format=v.format GROUP BY v.format ORDER BY outperformer_rate DESC, avg_rel_lift DESC LIMIT 40

examples.q: Which high-lift videos have the most negative audience reaction? Name two examples, with lift and sentiment shown separately.
examples.a:
Two high-lift videos draw the most negative reactions: the WSJ News first-impressions video and the Both Sides of the Tech upgrade-advice video.

1. "I Tried Apple's First Folding iPhone. Here Are 3 Takeaways." (WSJ News): lift 14.06 (relative lift 2.81) on 503,852 views. Net sentiment is -35 (18% positive, 53% negative, n=17).

2. "Apple Might Not Make Another iPhone Duo..." (Both Sides of the Tech): lift 29.76 (relative lift 5.95) on 10,120 views. Net sentiment is -27 (27% positive, 55% negative, n=11).

Only these two videos qualified. Both samples are small, especially the second at n=11, so treat the sentiment as directional. Lift and sentiment are separate measures here, and high reach doesn't mean the reaction was favorable.
examples.sql: WITH s AS (SELECT cm.video_id, COUNT(*) AS n_product_side, AVG(cm.sentiment='positive') AS pct_pos, AVG(cm.sentiment='negative') AS pct_neg FROM comments cm WHERE cm.lang='en' AND cm.trivial=0 AND cm.target IN ('product','price_value','apple_brand','competitor') GROUP BY cm.video_id HAVING COUNT(*)>=10) SELECT c.video_id, c.title, cr.name AS creator, c.format, p.views, ROUND(p.lift,3) AS lift, ROUND(p.rel_lift,3) AS rel_lift, p.outperformer, s.n_product_side, ROUND(s.pct_pos,3) AS pct_positive, ROUND(s.pct_neg,3) AS pct_negative, ROUND(s.pct_pos - s.pct_neg,3) AS net_sentiment FROM content c JOIN creators cr ON cr.channel_id=c.channel_id JOIN performance p ON p.video_id=c.video_id JOIN s ON s.video_id=c.video_id WHERE c.topic='duo' AND c.format!='official' AND p.outperformer=1 ORDER BY net_sentiment ASC, s.n_product_side DESC LIMIT 2

examples.q: Which audience topics are largest, and which are growing fastest this week?
examples.a:
Excitement and durability tests is the largest topic (n=281, 13% of Duo comments) and also gained the most share this week. Praise for the review is second (n=261, 12%), then Price and value (n=176) and Samsung Fold comparison (n=174).

Folding animation praise has the fastest raw growth, from 6 to 33 comments (+450%), but its base is tiny. Excitement and durability tests (28 to 145) and Samsung Fold comparison (17 to 86) grew about as fast on bigger numbers.

Total volume rose from 275 to 1,039 comments, so nearly every topic grew. Share change is more telling: Excitement and durability tests gained 3.8 points and Samsung Fold comparison 2.1. Inner screen and crease lost 6.6 points, and Duo comparisons and video content lost 4.3.

Caveat: last week's counts are small, so the growth rates swing a lot.
examples.sql: WITH sc AS (SELECT c.comment_id, c.topic_id, c.day_since_launch AS d FROM comments c JOIN content v ON v.video_id=c.video_id WHERE v.topic='duo' AND v.format!='official' AND c.lang='en' AND c.trivial=0), mx AS (SELECT max(d) AS m FROM sc), tot AS (SELECT count(*) AS t, sum(d>m-7) AS tw, sum(d<=m-7 AND d>m-14) AS pw FROM sc, mx), agg AS (SELECT topic_id, count(*) AS n_total, sum(d>m-7) AS n_this_week, sum(d<=m-7 AND d>m-14) AS n_prev_week FROM sc, mx WHERE topic_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY topic_id), r AS (SELECT t.topic_id, t.name, t.pool, t.origin, t.first_seen, a.n_total, round(a.n_total*1.0/tot.t,3) AS share_total, a.n_this_week, a.n_prev_week, round(a.n_this_week*1.0/tot.tw,3) AS share_this_week, round(a.n_prev_week*1.0/nullif(tot.pw,0),3) AS share_prev_week, round((a.n_this_week-a.n_prev_week)*1.0/nullif(a.n_prev_week,0),3) AS wow_growth, round(a.n_this_week*1.0/tot.tw - a.n_prev_week*1.0/nullif(tot.pw,0),3) AS share_change, tot.t AS n_scope_comments, tot.tw AS n_scope_this_week, tot.pw AS n_scope_prev_week FROM agg a JOIN topics t ON t.topic_id=a.topic_id, tot) SELECT *, rank() OVER (ORDER BY n_total DESC) AS size_rank, rank() OVER (ORDER BY wow_growth DESC) AS growth_rank FROM r ORDER BY n_total DESC LIMIT 40

examples.q: How does audience sentiment on the main product compare with the other products in the data?
examples.a:
Duo sits at a net sentiment of +17 (n=1,490 product-side comments across 126 videos), with 45% positive and 28% negative. That is clearly better than event coverage (-19, n=100) and the "other" topic (-12, n=67).

Only the competitor foldable scores higher, at +29 (n=45 across 3 videos; 49% positive, 20% negative). The iPhone 18 Pro is at +8, but n=13 across 2 videos is too small to read anything into.

Duo's figure is the only one built on a large sample. The competitor foldable, "other," and event numbers rest on small samples, so the gaps are directional. These are comment samples from non-official videos, and they show association, not cause.
examples.sql: SELECT c.topic, COUNT(DISTINCT c.video_id) AS n_videos, COUNT(*) AS n_product_side, ROUND(AVG(cm.sentiment='positive'),3) AS pct_positive, ROUND(AVG(cm.sentiment='neutral'),3) AS pct_neutral, ROUND(AVG(cm.sentiment='negative'),3) AS pct_negative, ROUND(AVG(cm.sentiment='positive')-AVG(cm.sentiment='negative'),3) AS net_sentiment, CASE WHEN COUNT(*)>=10 THEN 'ok' ELSE 'n<10' END AS n_check FROM comments cm JOIN content c ON c.video_id=cm.video_id WHERE cm.lang='en' AND cm.trivial=0 AND cm.target IN ('product','price_value','apple_brand','competitor') AND c.format!='official' GROUP BY c.topic ORDER BY (c.topic='duo') DESC, n_product_side DESC LIMIT 40

examples.q: What do people like most about iPhone Duo, and what do they criticise most?
examples.a:
Commenters like the anticipation and the planned durability tests most, and they criticise price and value most.

Liked: "Excitement and durability tests" has the most positive comments, 123 of 234 (n=234), a net sentiment of +35 (52.6% positive, 17.9% negative). That topic holds 30% of all positive comments. The folding and intro animation also scores well at +30 (n=89, 55.1% positive, 24.7% negative).

Criticised: "Price and value" draws the largest share of negative comments, 23.6%. It has 51 negative out of 151 (n=151), a net of +13 (47.0% positive, 33.8% negative). Many call the phone very expensive and compare it with cheaper foldables. The inner screen and crease follows (n=137, 34 negative, net +16).

Caveat: this is a sample of comments, and the same topics appear on both lists. Even the most criticised topic is net positive.
examples.sql: WITH base AS (SELECT c.sentiment, c.topic_id FROM comments c JOIN content v ON v.video_id=c.video_id WHERE v.topic='duo' AND v.format!='official' AND c.lang='en' AND c.trivial=0 AND c.target IN ('product','price_value')), t AS (SELECT b.topic_id, tp.name, tp.summary, COUNT(*) n_comments, SUM(b.sentiment='positive') n_pos, SUM(b.sentiment='negative') n_neg FROM base b JOIN topics tp ON tp.topic_id=b.topic_id GROUP BY b.topic_id), tot AS (SELECT SUM(n_pos) tp, SUM(n_neg) tn FROM t) SELECT * FROM (SELECT 'praise' side, t.name, t.summary, t.n_comments, t.n_pos, t.n_neg, ROUND(1.0*t.n_pos/t.n_comments,3) pos_share_in_topic, ROUND(1.0*t.n_neg/t.n_comments,3) neg_share_in_topic, ROUND(1.0*t.n_pos/tot.tp,3) share_of_all_positive FROM t, tot ORDER BY t.n_pos DESC LIMIT 6) UNION ALL SELECT * FROM (SELECT 'criticism' side, t.name, t.summary, t.n_comments, t.n_pos, t.n_neg, ROUND(1.0*t.n_pos/t.n_comments,3), ROUND(1.0*t.n_neg/t.n_comments,3), ROUND(1.0*t.n_neg/tot.tn,3) FROM t, tot ORDER BY t.n_neg DESC LIMIT 6)
